description: The catch game's words: short cards that fall one after another, each SAFE (the learner catches it) or a HAZARD (the learner lets it pass). One item is one reported decision; its id is a data-question-id row on the page, and its outcome codes are that row's data-measures, never in here. Ask the person for every rule and source you were not given.

title.description: The game's title, on its first screen and its debrief.

items.description: The cards, in the order they fall. Mix safe and hazard; keep their labels about the same length, so the length never gives the answer away. Each card falls in one of three lanes and has one outcome: caught, or passed.

id.description: The interaction id the LMS receives: ASCII, unique in the lecture, and the data-question-id of one row on the page. Take it from the client's alignment document; never invent it.

label.description: What falls, read in a second while it moves: two to four words, a behaviour or a thing, never a verdict («آمن», «خطر») that tells the answer.

kind.description: safe: catching it is right. hazard: letting it pass is right, and catching it costs a heart. The response the LMS receives is caught or passed, and the result says whether that fits the kind.

rule.description: Why, in one sentence: shown after a wrong act during play, and in the debrief.

source.description: The citation the learner reads under the rule («المصدر: …»). Ask the person; never invent it. Left empty, the release lists it as left for the person.

slots.description: Optional: the art hand's own pictures for the game's three picture slots (game.json names their sizes). Each value is a path under the lecture's assets, such as "../assets/hero.png"; a slot left out keeps the game's own placeholder.

hero.description: The character the learner moves along the bottom, seen from the front; transparent around it.

item.description: The picture every falling card carries, the SAME for safe and hazard cards, so the picture never gives the answer away; transparent around it.

background.description: The playfield behind the cards, tiled; opaque.
